body: Rogue Galaxy is Level-5's PlayStation 2 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 8 December 2005. Jaster Rogue begins as a young agricultural worker on an isolated planet before becoming involved with a spacefaring crew and a conflict that reaches across the galaxy. The adventure turns his wish for a wider life into a sequence of new worlds and companions. Exploration leads directly into active battles, keeping the journey close to the characters on screen. Its scale reflects Level-5's ambition to build a large original role-playing adventure for Sony's console.

Real-time combat allows the player to move and attack while companions take part around the controlled character. Character development and equipment provide work between encounters, while numerous optional activities extend the journey beyond the next story destination. A planet can therefore offer both a place in the main adventure and something worth returning to later. The structure encourages the player to treat the crew as an ongoing group whose abilities and equipment continue to develop. Progress is expressed through those preparations as well as the discovery of another part of the galaxy.

Akihiro Hino and Takeshi Akasaka directed the project, with Tomohito Nishiura composing its music. Development lasted more than three years and involved a larger team than Level-5 had previously used. An expanded Director's Cut became the basis of the 2007 North American and PAL releases, adding changes beyond the first Japanese edition. Reviewers praised the presentation and range of activities while responding less uniformly to the story and characters. The game brought Level-5's experience with expansive console adventures into an original space-fantasy setting, combining a long journey with many smaller diversions.
story_headings: Give the crew reasons to keep exploring
